Frequently Asked Questions
Do I have to move my site to Frase? No. Frase publishes into the CMS you already use — WordPress, Webflow, Sanity or Wix. Or publish to FraseCMS: an agent-ready CMS, hosted or headless, on your own domain, with WebMCP so AI assistants can read your pages and act on them. Either way your content stays yours and exports whenever you want it.
Does Frase monitor whether AI cites me? Yes. AI Visibility tracks where you show up across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, and Google AI on a daily cadence, and alerts you when your share of voice moves. AI Visibility is a separate feature from Content Guard.
Does Frase fix pages automatically? Content Guard watches your published pages for ranking and traffic decay in Google and drafts the fix. You approve each change. You can opt in to let Frase apply low-risk fixes automatically, but that stays your call.
How does Frase know my brand? Two ways. Frase builds a brand profile from the content you already have, and you can set it yourself in the Brand Hub: your tone, your rules, the terms you use and the ones you never want used. Every draft is written against that, then checked against the live results you are competing with.
Is Frase for agencies? Yes. On Scale, agencies get multi-site, multi-seat, exportable client-ready reports, and role-based access. White-label, branded client portals, and custom domains are available on Enterprise.
Does the free trial need a credit card? No. The trial runs for 7 days with no credit card required. You add billing only when you choose a plan.
Can I run Frase from my own agent or terminal? Bring your own agent. Frase runs where you already work — Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor, your own terminal — through the MCP server and CLI, on every plan, so it researches, drafts and publishes without leaving the tool you are in. Point it at your site and let it run.
Do I need to be an SEO expert to use Frase? No. Frase handles the research, drafts in your voice, and points to exactly what to improve before you publish. You bring the strategy and the judgment. Frase does the legwork.
Frase does the work.
You stay in charge.
Point Frase at your site and see what it finds. The fixes come written, and nothing goes live until you say so.

Frequently Asked Questions
What do I get in the 7-day free trial? Professional's full feature set, including the part most tools make you pay to reach: you can let the agent publish on its own during the trial. Turn it on for a content type, watch what it ships, and turn it off again if you don't like what you see. You also get the content calendar, internal linking, Frase's AI engines for content (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini), and AI Visibility on ChatGPT and Google AI. Quantities are capped at 5 articles, 50 audit pages, 25 AI prompts and up to 3 seats. No credit card to start.
What happens when I hit a monthly limit? On Starter, Frase holds at the limit until your cycle resets or you upgrade, so a surprise charge never happens. On Professional and Scale, you can switch on pay-as-you-go capacity and keep going. Professional adds $5 per extra article, $0.50 per audit page, and $0.25 per AI prompt. Scale adds $4, $0.40, and $0.20. Overages only apply if you turn them on, and they bill at the end of your cycle.
How do add-ons work? Extra seats run $29/mo each on Professional and Scale. Audit pages and AI generations come as pay-as-you-go capacity on those same plans. FraseCMS hosting is an add-on too: free with any plan, then $19/mo for Basic or $99/mo for Pro on top of it. Add what you need, when you need it. The sticker price is your floor, not a number that creeps up behind your back.
Can I change plans later? Yes. Upgrade whenever you want and the change is prorated on the spot. Downgrade and it takes hold at your next billing cycle. Choose yearly billing and 20% comes off the monthly rate.
What does Content Guard do, and what stays in my control? When a published page starts losing Google rank or traffic, Content Guard writes the fix and republishes it to your CMS once you approve. Approval is the default on every change. You can opt in to let Frase ship low-risk fixes on their own, and that switch is always yours to flip back. AI Visibility is a separate feature: it monitors AI engines and alerts you, and it never touches your content.
Which CMS platforms does Frase publish to? Frase publishes to WordPress, Webflow, Sanity, and Wix, or hosts the content for you on FraseCMS — an agent-ready CMS, hosted or headless, with WebMCP so AI assistants can read your pages and act on them.
How much does FraseCMS cost? The free tier is included with any Frase plan: 100,000 page views a month and 25 GB of bandwidth. Basic and Pro are add-ons on top of your plan. Basic is $19/mo for 250,000 page views, a subdirectory of your own site if you want one, and no Frase badge. Pro is $99/mo for a million page views. Yearly billing saves two months on either. Past the cap, the free tier pauses until the month resets; Basic and Pro keep serving at $1.00 and $0.50 per extra 1,000 page views, with a spend cap set at your base price by default, so overage cannot silently run away. A page view counts each time a page is served to a reader or pulled through the API.
Is Scale enough for my agency, or do I need Enterprise? For most agencies, Scale is plenty: up to 10 domains, 5 seats with roles, client-ready reports you can export, all self-serve. Turning one piece of content into posts for every channel starts on Professional. The line is white-label reports or a branded client portal. The moment you need one of those, that is Enterprise. Talk to sales and we will set it up.
What can I realistically expect Frase to do? Frase produces real, optimized content, surfaces the gaps in the pages you already have, and moves your in-app SEO, GEO, and AI-visibility scores as you apply the fixes. Rankings and AI citations are the slow part. They build over the weeks after you publish, so Frase shows you the work going out and tracks the signals coming back. What Frase will not do is promise you a ranking or a citation inside a 7-day window.
Frase does the work.
You stay in charge.
Point Frase at your site and see what it finds. The fixes come written, and nothing goes live until you say so.

An answer engine and a demand sensor in one
Frase Answers helps the visitor in front of you and helps the writer behind you. It answers the question now, remembers it so your content can answer it for everyone next, and widens the lens to what teams across your industry are asking too.
Answers visitors in plain language
Frase Answers reads from your published pages and responds to a visitor's question conversationally, so people get a direct answer instead of a search box and a list of links.
Cites your own pages
Every answer links back to the page it came from, so visitors can read the full source and you keep the trust of an answer that's grounded in your real content, not a guess.
Captures first‑party demand
Frase logs every question a visitor actually typed, in their own words, so you get a demand signal that's cleaner than keyword-tool guesses or scraped engine data.
Turns demand into the next page
Frase clusters repeated questions into content signals with a count and a suggested title, so a gap your visitors keep hitting becomes the brief your writer opens next.
Shows what your industry is asking
Beyond your own visitors, Frase surfaces the questions trending across teams in your industry on Frase, ranked gaps-first, so you can write for demand you'd never catch from your own traffic. It's an anonymized cohort of your industry — the insights you need, never named companies.
Benchmarks you against teams like yours
Frase shows the peer-median outcome — how teams in your industry tend to rank and get mentioned by AI — beside yours, so you can see where you stand. It's what's observed across teams who acted, not a guarantee, and identities stay private.
Reads from the content you already have
Frase Answers works from your existing pages, so it gets more useful as you publish, and there's no separate knowledge base to build or keep in sync by hand.
Free to start on your site
There's a free Answers tier for your site, with a paid add-on when your conversation volume grows, so you can put the front door on your pages and see what visitors ask before you commit.
A chatbot answers and forgets. Frase Answers answers and learns.
A bolted-on chatbot helps the visitor in front of it and loses everything the moment they leave. Frase Answers keeps the question and turns it into content, so every conversation makes your site better at answering the next one.
The fragmented way With Frase
A chatbot answers from a separate knowledge base you have to build and maintain. Frase Answers reads from the pages you already publish, and improves as you write more.
Questions disappear once the chat closes, so you never learn what people wanted. Frase captures every question in the visitor's own words as first-party demand.
You guess at the next blog post from keyword tools and scraped data. Frase clusters real visitor questions into a ranked list of pages to write.
The chatbot and your content workflow live in two unconnected tools. Answers feeds the same loop that researches, drafts, and publishes the page.

Frequently Asked Questions
What is Frase Answers? Frase Answers is a conversational widget you add to your site. It answers your visitors' questions from your own published content, with citations back to the pages the answer came from, and it captures every question in the visitor's own words. So it helps the visitor now and gives you a demand signal for what to write next. It's live and available today.
Where do the answers come from? From your own content. Frase Answers reads the pages you publish and grounds every response in them, then links back to the source page. It doesn't invent an answer from the open web, so what it tells a visitor is what your site actually says. The more you publish, the more it can answer.
What does "what your industry is asking" mean — is it my competitors? No. Frase Answers shows the questions trending across teams in your industry who use Frase — an anonymized cohort that gives you the insights you need, never named companies. It surfaces the gaps first: the questions your industry keeps asking that your pages don't answer yet. It tells you what people are asking, not what other companies are writing or publishing. Add any gap to your signals and Frase drafts the page.
How is Frase Answers different from AI Visibility tracking? They face opposite directions. Frase Answers is on your site and captures the questions your visitors ask you, and it widens that to the questions trending across teams in your industry. AI Visibility is a separate feature that monitors what AI search engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and Gemini say and cite about your brand out on the web, and how your share of voice compares. Answers tells you what to write; AI Visibility tracks where you show up after you publish. Many teams run both.
Does Frase Answers change my content on its own? No. Frase Answers surfaces demand; it does not write or publish anything by itself. When a question keeps coming up, Frase turns it into a content signal you can accept, and then the agent researches and drafts the page for your review. Nothing goes live without you.
Is there a free version? Yes. There's a free Answers tier you can put on your site, with a paid add-on for higher conversation volume as your traffic grows. You can add the widget and see what your visitors ask before you decide to scale it up.
Do I have to move my content to use it? No. Frase Answers reads from the content you already publish, on the CMS you already run, whether that's WordPress, Webflow, Sanity, Wix, or FraseCMS. You don't migrate anything to put the front door on your site.
Answer your visitors. Learn what to write next.
Start a trial, add Frase Answers to your site, and it starts answering visitors from your content and logging what they ask. Within the trial you'll have a working answer engine on your pages and a real list of questions your visitors want answered, not a vague promise of more leads someday.

Briefing a piece usually means a SERP tool, a keyword tool, a questions tool, and a doc to glue them together by hand. Frase keeps the whole pass in one place and ends with something you can write from.

Frequently Asked Questions
What does Frase research, exactly? For a topic, Frase reads the pages already ranking and breaks down how each one is built, gathers the questions real searchers ask from People Also Ask and forums, expands the related keywords, and flags the gaps competitors leave open. It assembles all of it into a structured brief you can hand to the writer.
Does Frase build the brief, or just hand me data? It builds the brief. Frase consolidates the SERP breakdown, questions, keywords, and gaps into a structured outline with headings and sections. You can hand it straight to the writer for a first draft, or pin and adjust what makes the cut before you do. You decide what goes in.
How is this different from a standalone keyword or SERP tool? Standalone tools hand you raw data (keyword lists, volumes, SERP positions) and leave the synthesis to you. Frase is a content research tool that ends in output: it runs the research and turns it into a brief in the same flow, then passes that brief to the writer. Research and drafting do not live in separate tools.
Can I run research by just asking the Frase Agent? Yes. Ask the Frase Agent to research a topic and it runs the analysis under the hood, then returns a brief. You can refine it in the same conversation — change the angle, adjust the outline, or ask for more on a section. Frase proposes; you approve what goes in.
Does Frase research in languages other than English? Yes. Set a target language and country for the run, and Frase pulls the SERP, the questions, and the competitor breakdown for that locale, so the brief reflects how searchers in that market actually phrase intent rather than a translated approximation.
What happens to the brief after I build it? The brief hands off to the Frase writer, which drafts the page in your brand voice. From there the editor scores the draft for SEO and for AI search (GEO) so you can see what to improve before you publish. Research, brief, draft, and optimize stay in one continuous flow. See SEO content optimization for the scoring step.
Do I have to redo the research for every related topic? No. Frase reuses overlapping research, so when you brief a related topic the second run starts from what it already gathered instead of fetching everything again. Related pieces come together noticeably faster.

Frequently Asked Questions
What is a topic cluster? A topic cluster is a pillar page covering a broad subject plus the supporting pages that answer its subtopics, all linked together. Covering a topic this thoroughly signals depth to Google and to readers, and it helps the whole group rank rather than a single page fighting alone. Frase gives you a map to plan and build that structure on purpose.
Does Frase build my clusters automatically? Frase proposes, you decide. When you add a piece of content or a brief, Frase matches its topic and keywords against your existing clusters and suggests where it fits, with the reason. You accept the suggestion, pick a different cluster, or leave it unclustered. Nothing is reorganized without your say-so, and the bulk organizer even previews its moves before applying any.
How does Frase find content gaps in a cluster? Frase reads the results already ranking for your topic and surfaces the questions and subtopics your cluster has not covered yet. Those gaps show up as opportunities you can turn into a brief in one click, so you fill the holes that matter instead of guessing what to write next.
Can I see how my content is connected? Yes. The cluster map is a visual view of your pillars, supporting content, briefs, and anything still unclustered. You can see the shape of each topic at a glance and tell which pieces anchor a cluster and which support it.
How do I create content to fill a gap? Click a missing subtopic and Frase builds a brief from it, then you research and write the page in the same workspace, in your brand voice. The new piece lands in the cluster it belongs to, so the structure stays intact as you publish.
Does cluster content help my pages get cited by AI search? Thorough topic coverage helps with both Google and AI search. As you write each piece, Frase shows a GEO score alongside the SEO score, so you can see how the page reads to AI engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini. See GEO content optimization for the full picture on getting cited.
Does Frase work in languages other than English? Yes. You can plan clusters, research, and write content in more than 70 languages, so teams building authority in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, and beyond use Frase the same way they do in English.
